get.summary: Everything the comparison page needs in one call: run, model, per-site horizon, series, windows, metrics, criteria
get.description: Defaults: default run, every site of the run, the whole run range, data step (3600 s), max_points 10000, horizon_step_deg 1, criteria_hours 24,72,168, include all. Series are decimated per site to <= max_points while keeping both samples around every visibility transition (see DatasetSeries). Windows / metrics / criteria are computed from the full-resolution windows over the requested range (whole run -> exactly summary.csv / windows.json). Payload limit: the series points of all sites together (regular + transition samples, exactly as returned) must be <= 50000 (about 4.5 MB of JSON, ~1 MB gzip), else 422 OUT_OF_RANGE with the numbers and a fitting max_points; first check (before any read): sites x min(max_points, n_samples / k) - so a call with no parameters on a 23-site 5-year run is 422; e.g. all 23 sites x 31 days hourly = 17 112 points is fine, the whole 5-year run for many sites needs max_points <= 50000 / n_sites or fewer site_ids (a large step_s alone may not be enough: transition samples are always kept). Windows and horizon bytes are not counted. Without `series` in include there is no point limit (whole run, 23 sites: ~0.7 MB, ~0.2 s); a whole-run series for all sites takes ~8 s, so request series for <= 1 year or a few sites. A range partly outside the run is clamped (coverage = partial); no overlap -> 422 OUT_OF_RANGE. Unknown site id -> 404 SITE_NOT_FOUND.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: Run to read; default = the run flagged is_default (GET /api/v1/runs)

parameters.name: site_ids
parameters.description: Comma separated site ids (max 100, duplicates ignored, response keeps this order). Default: every site of the run in sites.json order.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Inclusive start (default: run start). Snapped DOWN to the sample grid.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: EXCLUSIVE end (default: run end). Snapped UP to the sample grid. A range partly outside the run is clamped (coverage = partial); no overlap -> 422 OUT_OF_RANGE.

parameters.name: step_s
parameters.description: Desired spacing of the series, seconds (default = the data step, 3600). The server keeps every k-th sample, k = floor(step_s / data step), PLUS both samples around every Sun/Earth visibility transition, and raises k further if needed so a site never exceeds max_points. The spacing actually used is series.step_s.

parameters.name: max_points
parameters.description: Cap on series points per site (default and max 10000), transition samples included. Also: the series points of all sites together must be <= 50000, else 422 OUT_OF_RANGE.

parameters.name: horizon_step_deg
parameters.description: Azimuth step of the returned horizon curve: 1 (default, 361 points 0..360) or 0.5 (721 points, ~4 KB per site). The stored silhouette is 0.5 deg for most sites: 1 POINT-SAMPLES it at whole degrees (the half-degree samples are dropped, so a narrow peak between two whole degrees is not drawn and a Sun / Earth marker can appear on the wrong side of the drawn curve near it). Only 0.5 is exactly consistent with sun_visible / earth_visible; prefer it for rim sites (or all sites) when drawing markers against the horizon.

parameters.name: criteria_hours
parameters.description: Comma separated minimum durations in hours (> 0, max 30; deduplicated and sorted ascending). Each one is evaluated against longest_both_h.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma separated parts of each site to return: horizon, series, windows, metrics, criteria (default: all). Omitted parts are absent from sites[].

get.description: Probed at startup and cached (CAPABILITIES_TTL_S, default 600 s; `checked_at`). `?refresh=true` probes again (at most every 30 s). Use it to enable / disable UI options: a job type with available = false answers 501 JOB_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE, an option the server lacks (dem trek without files, near_exclusion_m without CLI support) 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE. Network reachability is null when the probe is disabled.

post.summary: Start a Python job (async): custom_site, precompute, analyse, alt_dates_python, check, validate, ...
post.description: Body = CreateJobRequest, discriminated on `type` (one schema per job type; GET /api/v1/capabilities lists the types this server runs - others answer 501 JOB_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE). 202 = queued, or an identical job is already queued/running: you are then subscribed to it (cached: true, same job_id; poll `poll` every 1-2 s; `Location` header = the same URL). 200 = an identical job already succeeded (cached: true). 429 TOO_MANY_JOBS when this client (IP) already waits on JOB_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_CLIENT (default 2) queued/running jobs; 429 QUEUE_FULL when JOB_QUEUE_MAX jobs wait. start snaps down / end snaps up to whole hours. When succeeded, use result.run_id with the normal endpoints. Measured on the dev machine (1 site, hourly, spice + pgda + raymarch, PGDA tiles of the area already cached): POST -> succeeded in ~14 s for 1 month and ~19 s for 1 year (precompute 11-18 s, import 1-3 s). The first job in a polar area not yet cached also downloads PGDA tiles and can take minutes.

post.summary: Alternative landing dates for one site (slip calendar)
post.description: Synchronous (<= 30 s, ~0.5 s typical; identical requests are served from a 7-day cache, header `x-lunarnav-cache: hit|miss|shared`). No feasible date = 200 with empty candidates + rejected_by. mission_h not a multiple of the step -> 422 BAD_MISSION_LENGTH; earliest before the run start -> 422 OUT_OF_RANGE (min_earliest); latest + mission_h past the run end -> 422 OUT_OF_RANGE (max_latest); latest < earliest -> 400. Works on custom job runs too (run_id = job_...).

result.description: Rise / set times are known to one data step: a start after the range start can add up to one step, an end not cut by the range end (clipped_end false) can remove up to one step; a start at the range start and a clipped end are exact inside the range. meets = every possible true in-range length >= minimum_hours, below = every possible length < minimum_hours, else borderline. With both edges sampled: borderline <=> |value_h - minimum_hours| < one data step; with both edges cut by the range: meets or below, never borderline.

DatasetSeries.description: Columnar series (all arrays have the same length, <= max_points). Decimation keeps sample 0, every k-th sample, the last sample, and the samples i-1 and i around every change of sun_visible or earth_visible, so a rise or set is never lost (exact to +- one data step). When decimated, t is IRREGULAR (transition samples sit between the regular ones): plot by timestamp. The last sample is range.end - range.step_s (end is exclusive). Use the *_visible flags (or windows) for visibility: they are NOT el > 0 (Sun upper limb, Earth centre + clearance, terrain horizon, mast height).
